route.description: A = the public definition changes (a slot, property or event is added, removed or changes meaning) and the molecule must be rebuilt. B = a minor change: appearance, a code defect, wording. C = the molecule is a shell AND the behaviour to change lives in its parent. D = the request is not about changing this molecule.

rationale.description: One or two sentences, in the user's language, saying WHY this route. It is shown to the user, and on route D it is the whole answer they get.

expectedArtifacts.description: Which artifacts the change is expected to touch. EMPTY on routes A and D — A hands the work over to a rebuild and D writes nothing. At least one on routes B and C.

definitionElements.description: Only on route A: the named slots, properties or events that are added, removed or change meaning, e.g. 'slot Detail', 'property pageSize', 'event rowClick'. Empty on every other route. This list is what pre-fills the rebuild clarification, so a vague entry costs the user a round trip.
